chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfaly, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah, from his forefathers (peace be upon them), who said:
The prayer in the Sacred Masjid equals one hundred thousand prayers.

key_terms.الْمَسْجِدِ الْحَرَامِ: The Sacred Masjid (specifically referring to the Kaaba in Mecca)

ai.seo_question: What is the reward multiplier for prayer in the Sacred Masjid?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) highlights the unique spiritual gravity of the Kaaba, distinguishing it from other sanctified sites like Jerusalem or Medina. While some scholars debate whether this 'one hundred thousand' is literal or symbolic of immense reward, it underscores the concept of *fadilah* (superiority) inherent in the holiest site in Islam. This merit is often contextualized alongside the Prophet's night journey, linking the physical location to divine selection and cosmic significance.
